summary: node-telegram-sockets@1.1.2: static keyword co-occurrence, no confirmed installer harm
details: Package is a Telegram Bot API client fork. Static keyword patterns matched on co-occurrence of `require('fs')`/`require('http')`/`require('https')` with `fs.readFileSync` in lib/telegramWebHook.js and src/telegramWebHook.js, and on the token `ping` in lib/telegram.js, src/telegram.js, and test/telegram.js. The `ping` matches are consistent with Telegram Bot API method names (e.g., `getMe`/health endpoints) or string occurrences in a Telegram client library rather than ICMP/host reconnaissance. The fs+http co-occurrence in the webhook module is consistent with a standard webhook server pattern that reads a TLS certificate/key from disk to bind an HTTPS listener — the documented purpose of a Telegram bot webhook. No hardcoded attacker C2 endpoint, browser credential enumeration, wallet/extension lookup, seed-phrase scanner, ~/.npmrc/~/.aws/~/.ssh reader, or known-bad dropper infrastructure was identified. No install/postinstall/preinstall lifecycle script harm was identified. The pattern matches are weak (keyword co-occurrence in a Telegram client library) and do not, on their own, demonstrate exfiltration of installer-side data to an attacker-controlled destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
